newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Hyperactive FTSE to stay near 4,350 level.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Hyperactive FTSE to stay near 4,350 level.

text.p: Strains in the London stock market will be evident on Friday from a combination of investor anxiety over interest rates as well as a double-witching session with the expiry of stock index futures and options -- leading to another hyperactive day, technical analysts said.
Up to Thursday's close the index had lost 186 points or four percent -- on a closing basis -- since its peak at 4,444.3 on March 11 so it should be near to securing a temporary foothold.
This should mean the FTSE 100 index may be able to finish the day near the 4,250 level today, they added.
By 0809 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 3.2 at 4,254.9.

With all the excitement on offer from the derivatives market today after the market's recent tumble, a technical bounce by the FTSE is possible but it will be by a meagre amount and will provide little consolation for those who had bought shares near the top, analysts said.
A daily bar chart of the index since its peak hiighlight how the market's demise but its short-term oscillators such as the 10 day momentum indicates the FTSE is close to a turning point.
The 10 day momentum is a measure of the rate of change of prices over a moving 10 day period and this indicator is now at its lowest point since November implying a very oversold state.

But from trend analysis -- from which forecasts are made from observing the direction of market prices rather than from any derivative of them -- indicates the overall market trend remains down at least for the near-term, analysts said.

This applies equally well to leading stock markets in Europe as well as the U.S. which are all trending down but may be able to find some support after recent falls as they wait for a decision on U.S. interest rates on March 25, analysts added.
